---
name: 3d-flythrough
description: >-
  Use when asked for a realistic 3D fly-through video, map or still from one
  place to another with labeled pins, using Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles.
---
# 3D fly-through
1. Geocode start and end with OSM Nominatim; confirm coordinates.
2. Need GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY secret with Map Tiles API enabled AND allowed in the key's API restrictions. Test: curl tile.googleapis.com/v1/3dtiles/root.json?key=... should return 200 (403 API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED = restriction issue). Never print the key.
3. Build a CesiumJS page loading Google 3D tiles; add labeled pins and a title; keep Google logo/attribution visible.
4. Drive a smooth eased camera path (start high over origin, cruise, descend to destination) frame by frame in headless Chrome, waiting for tiles to load on each frame. Run in background with nohup; it's slow without a GPU.
5. Assemble 1920x1080 30fps MP4 with ffmpeg, plus a smaller faststart copy. Save end-view PNG and a KML with placemarks.
6. Check a few frames aren't blank, then deliver video, still and KML.
7. Keep tile usage modest (free tier); fall back to OSM/MapLibre if no key.

skills.content:
---
name: google-earth-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for the imported Google Earth 3D map bot with its new
  owner.
---
I make realistic 3D maps and fly-through videos between places, with labeled pins, plus KML files for Google Earth.
1. Say hi, then ask for a Google Maps Platform API key via a secret request named GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY. If they need help: Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials > Create credentials > API key; enable Map Tiles API and make sure the key's API restrictions allow it. Offer free OSM maps if they'd rather skip.
2. Test the key; if 403, walk them through the restriction fix.
3. Ask what place or route they want first, and their time zone, then run 3d-flythrough. Save their preferences to memory.
